extracted.intended_audience: C and C++ developers, DevOps/CI engineers, teams and organizations evaluating or using a native package manager
extracted.subtask_description: High-level product/feature overview of Conan 2.0 as an open-source package manager for C and C++: what it supports, integrations, hosting options, and claimed benefits for teams and CI pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal and portable
rubrics_metrics.description: Conan is universal and portable. It works in all operating systems including Windows, Linux, OSX, FreeBSD, and others, and it can target any platform, including desktop, server, and cross-building for mobile (Android and iOS), as well as embedded and bare metal devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Conan to target many OSes and platforms; supports cross-building scenarios for mobile and embedded targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with other tools and build systems
rubrics_metrics.description: It integrates with other tools like Docker, MinGW, WSL, and with all build systems such as CMake, MSBuild, Makefiles, Meson, SCons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conan can even integrate with any proprietary build systems — applicable when embedding into existing toolchains or CI flows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open source and free with active maintainers/community
rubrics_metrics.description: Conan is open source and completely free. Conan is developed by a full team of full-time maintainers who support many thousands of users, alongside an active and awesome community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project backing and community support are presented as part of its reliability and long-term viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native integration with Artifactory and private hosting
rubrics_metrics.description: It has native integration with JFrog Artifactory, including the free Artifactory Community Edition for Conan, enabling developers to host their own private packages on their own server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended server: Artifactory Community Edition for C and C++; features include WebUI, advanced authentication and permissions, REST API, generic CLI and generic repositories to host source or binary artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage any number of binaries and configurations
rubrics_metrics.description: Conan can manage any number of different binaries and different build configurations, including different architectures, compilers, compiler versions, runtimes, C++ standard library, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When binaries are not available for one configuration, they can be built from sources on-demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent create/upload/download workflows across platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Conan can create, upload and download binaries with the same commands and flows on every platform, saving lots of time in development and continuous integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform commands reduce CI complexity and platform-specific scripting; emphasizes portability of workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized public repository (ConanCenter) with metadata and precompiled binaries
rubrics_metrics.description: ConanCenter is the central repository where you can search and discover all the available open source Conan packages created by the community. It includes recipe and configuration information, and makes it easy to see package metadata in the UI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ConanCenter contains more than a thousand popular open source libraries packages, with many pre-compiled binaries for mainstream compiler versions and platforms — useful for fast adoption and avoiding local builds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speeds up development and reduces build times
rubrics_metrics.description: Conan integration enabled a 10x reduction in our development compile-test cycle and release build times; helped reduce full build time by over 40 minutes in customer stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimonials highlight concrete time savings and cost reductions (e.g., reduced AWS bill); use Conan to produce binary artifacts to shorten developer build times and CI cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitates modularization, dependency management, and easier maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizing codebase into multiple packages enabled easier maintenance. The dependency graph visualizer gives an overview of all modules/packages and their contribution to the complete project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables modular distributions (example: modular Boost C++ Libraries), easier reuse, and simpler testing/prototyping workflows by adding package lines to a text file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enables rapid prototyping and multi-library testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Conan arrived just in time to enable us to test multiple networking, logging, and cryptography libraries simply by adding lines to a text file; when mastering a library, invest into a single cross-platform package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports rapid iteration and later consolidation into cross-platform packages to avoid repeated builds by individual developers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable to enterprise and large-scale workflows
rubrics_metrics.description: Used by enterprises (TomTom, Mercedes-Benz R&D, GitHub Enterprise customers) to establish continuous delivery pipelines and to streamline development for distributed teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims suitability from small teams to big enterprises; includes features and integrations expected in production-grade CI/CD environments.
